inputs.original_text: Abinader’s government is putting the Dominican Republic on a path shaped by OECD “global standards,” with Roberto Álvarez and Mathias Cormann signing an agreement in Paris on 25 March 2026 to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption is worthwhile, but it should strengthen accountable Dominican institutions—not become a pretext for handing more influence to international bureaucrats. The real test will be whether this produces honest government at home, rather than another polished agreement abroad.
inputs.modified_text: Abinader’s government has signed an agreement in Paris with OECD chief Mathias Cormann to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption matters, but handing international bureaucrats a bigger role in shaping Dominican policy is no guarantee of honest government. The test is whether the country strengthens its own accountable institutions and serves its people—not whether it adopts another set of “global standards.”
